S334.scope: The SHA-256 message-digest size: what FIPS 180-4 states the SHA-256 output length is and where that statement sits; not the other SHA-2 variants and not the preimage-resistance arguments
S334.anchor: section 6.2 SHA-256, printed page 21 (PDF page 26 of 36); the document PDF fetched 2026-11-05, 833315 bytes, raw SHA256 0455b406d89648d20cbde375561e19c245b9815e894164c2670772e3d54deb82; the CSRC landing page https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final answers HTTP 200 but serves only metadata and links this PDF
S334.teaches: The standard states that the final result of SHA-256 is a 256-bit message digest, and repeats that the resulting 256-bit message digest of the message M is the eight-word hash value, so a SHA-256 digest is 256 bits wide

S335.scope: Documented subprocess timeout semantics: which functions raise TimeoutExpired when the timeout elapses, and what happens to the child process, for run(), call(), Popen.wait(timeout) and Popen.communicate(timeout); not the Windows-specific or pipes-deadlock behaviour
S335.anchor: Exceptions (raise on expiry) and the run(), Popen.wait(timeout), Popen.communicate() and call() entries; the page fetched 2026-11-05 served Python 3.15.2 documentation, 208648 bytes, raw SHA256 ff3cca533d01e1b06eb5d3d541ef0e6e32b1d755fc9419afc287bfeddd33e503
S335.teaches: Functions and methods that accept a timeout parameter raise TimeoutExpired if the timeout expires before the process exits; run() additionally kills and waits for the child and re-raises TimeoutExpired after the child has terminated, whereas Popen.communicate() on its own does not kill the child, and call() inherits its timeout behaviour from Popen.wait(timeout)

notes: docs.python.org/3/ is a rolling URL: the same URL serves a different Python 3.x document over time, so the anchor cell must carry the fetched byte count and sha256, not just the URL.
